findings.evidence_redacted: logger.info(f"OpenStack connection successful. Token acquired: {<REDACTED:token_prefix>}...")
findings.impact: A Keystone token prefix is emitted to the application log at INFO level on every successful connection, exposing auth material to anyone with log-read access.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with: logger.info("OpenStack connection successful. Token acquired.")

findings.evidence_redacted: verify_ssl = False  # HTTP mode — the default when OS_AUTH_PROTOCOL is not set
findings.impact: Every deployment without explicit HTTPS + OS_CACERT runs with verify=False on all service endpoints, enabling MITM interception of credentials and tokens in transit.
findings.suggested_fix: Default OS_AUTH_PROTOCOL to https. Require ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=true as an explicit env-var opt-in. Never set verify=False silently.

findings.evidence_redacted: headers = {'X-Auth-Token': <REDACTED:keystone_token>}; requests.get(f"http://...", headers=headers)
findings.impact: Live Keystone auth token sent in X-Auth-Token header over hardcoded http:// via raw requests calls, bypassing the SDK transport layer. Occurs in 4 call sites.
findings.suggested_fix: Use SDK methods (conn.orchestration.stacks()) instead of raw requests. If unavoidable, use os_auth_protocol variable and validate TLS.

findings.evidence_redacted: conn.identity.delete_project(project)  # no confirm parameter
findings.impact: An LLM misinterpretation or prompt-injection can permanently delete an entire OpenStack project and all associated resources with a single tool call.
findings.suggested_fix: Add confirm: bool = False to set_project. Return dry-run details when confirm=False. Execute only when confirm=True.

findings.evidence_redacted: conn.compute.force_delete_server(server)  # or delete_server, no confirm
findings.impact: Both delete_server and force_delete_server are exposed as MCP tool actions with no confirmation parameter, enabling irreversible instance destruction from an LLM call.
findings.suggested_fix: Add confirm: bool = False. Gate both delete paths on confirm=True. Return dry-run info when confirm=False.

findings.evidence_redacted: 'private_key': getattr(keypair, 'private_key', None)
findings.impact: SSH private key injected directly into the LLM context window via tool response. May appear in conversation logs, session transcripts, or be exfiltrated via prompt injection.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove private_key from tool response. Inform user to download key through a secure out-of-band channel.

findings.evidence_redacted: conn.volume.delete_volume(volume, force=kwargs.get('force', False))  # no confirm
findings.impact: Volume deletion is irreversible. Force-deleting an attached volume can corrupt the guest filesystem. No confirmation gate exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Add confirm: bool = False gate to the tool. Gate both normal and force-delete on confirm=True.

findings.evidence_redacted: conn.network.delete_network(network)  # no confirm, callable via bulk filter
findings.impact: Network deletion cascades to subnets, ports, and floating-IP associations. Filter-based bulk deletion can wipe all matching networks with a single call.
findings.suggested_fix: Add confirm: bool = False and dry_run: bool = True default for filter-based operations.

findings.evidence_redacted: set_heat_stack(stack_names="...", action="delete")  # no confirm parameter
findings.impact: Heat stack deletion recursively deletes all managed resources (instances, networks, volumes). Irreversible without confirmation gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Add confirm: bool = False gate.

findings.evidence_redacted: set_image(image_names="...", action="delete")  # no confirm, bulk operation
findings.impact: Image deletion is irreversible. A single broad pattern could wipe all base images needed for instance provisioning.
findings.suggested_fix: Add confirm: bool = False gate, especially for bulk/filter-based operations.

findings.evidence_redacted: set_keypair(action="delete", name_contains="...")  # no confirm
findings.impact: Bulk keypair deletion revokes SSH access to all instances using those keys, potentially locking out all operators.
findings.suggested_fix: Add confirm: bool = False gate.

findings.evidence_redacted: conn.compute.evacuate_server(server, **evacuate_params)  # no confirm
findings.impact: Calling evacuate on a running instance on a healthy host can cause data corruption or unexpected VM restart.
findings.suggested_fix: Add confirm: bool = False gate.

findings.evidence_redacted: logger.warning("WARNING: streamable-http mode without authentication enabled!")  # server still starts
findings.impact: When REMOTE_AUTH_ENABLE is unset, the HTTP transport server accepts all connections without a Bearer token, exposing all tools including destructive ones.
findings.suggested_fix: Default auth_enable=True for HTTP transport. Require REMOTE_AUTH_ENABLE=false for explicit opt-out.

findings.evidence_redacted: except Exception as e: ... return False  # swallows 401/403
findings.impact: HTTP 401/403 and network timeouts are silently converted to False, preventing operators from distinguishing auth failures from legitimate cross-project denials.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-raise HTTP 401/403 exceptions. Use a custom AuthCheckError sentinel for auth failures vs False for genuine cross-project denial.

findings.evidence_redacted: 'email': getattr(user, 'email', 'N/A')  # PII returned in bulk
findings.impact: User email addresses (PII) returned in bulk to the LLM context window, accessible in conversation logs and via prompt injection.
findings.suggested_fix: Omit email from default response. Add include_email: bool = False opt-in parameter.

findings.evidence_redacted: "system_scope": system_scope  # admin-level privilege topology returned to LLM
findings.impact: System-scoped role assignments (indicating admin-level privileges) exposed in LLM context, enabling privilege topology mapping via prompt injection.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter out scope_type=system assignments from default response or redact user_id for system-scoped assignments.

findings.evidence_redacted: f"http://{<REDACTED:internal_host>}:{port}/v1/{<REDACTED:project_id>}/stacks"
findings.impact: Even with OS_AUTH_PROTOCOL=https, these raw requests calls always use http://, sending tokens over plaintext. Occurs in 6 call sites.
findings.suggested_fix: Use os_auth_protocol variable to construct URL. Migrate to SDK transport.

findings.evidence_redacted: instance_names: str  # passed directly to SDK without UUID validation
findings.impact: Unvalidated string inputs passed to OpenStack SDK. In the MCP threat model, prompt-injection attacks could supply crafted strings to probe internal API behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Add UUID_RE = re.compile(r'^[0-9a-f]{8}-...-[0-9a-f]{12}$', re.I) and validate all *_id parameters before SDK calls.

findings.evidence_redacted: all_servers = list(conn.compute.servers(details=True))  # unbounded
findings.impact: A single get_service_status call fetches all resource types without pagination. In large deployments this causes memory exhaustion and API gateway timeouts.
findings.suggested_fix: Add MAX_RESOURCE_PAGE_SIZE = 200 constant and paginate all list calls using limit/marker parameters.

findings.evidence_redacted: conn.identity.create_project(...)  # gated only by ALLOW_MODIFY_OPERATIONS
findings.impact: Project creation is a Keystone admin operation. The LLM can create arbitrary new projects if the service account has admin role.
findings.suggested_fix: Require a separate admin_confirm parameter matching a server-side configured token for admin operations.

findings.evidence_redacted: conn.identity.create_role(name=role_name)  # role_name unvalidated
findings.impact: Could trigger creation of a role with a name colliding with a built-in role or exploiting string matching in third-party RBAC tooling.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate role_name against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$. Log role creation at WARN level as a security event.

findings.evidence_redacted: set_quota(cores=999, ram=9999999)  # no bounds validation
findings.impact: Quota manipulation enables resource exhaustion attacks against other tenants. No upper bounds or confirmation for large increases.
findings.suggested_fix: Add per-parameter maximum bounds. Require confirm=True for increases exceeding a configured threshold.

findings.evidence_redacted: if not resource_project_id: return True  # fail-open for missing project_id
findings.impact: Resources missing project_id due to API version mismatch or SDK bug are granted access unconditionally instead of defaulting to deny.
findings.suggested_fix: Default to return False (deny) when project_id cannot be determined, unless resource type is in an explicit allowlist.

findings.evidence_redacted: except Exception as e:  # orphaned outside try block — unreachable
findings.impact: Genuine exceptions from set_compute_agents are not caught as intended, causing unhandled propagation.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the orphaned except block and ensure the enclosing try covers all relevant statements.

findings.evidence_redacted: "openstacksdk>=4.1.0,<=4.11.0"  # 10 minor versions; requests unpinned
findings.impact: Without an exact pin and committed lock file, a compromised mirror could serve a malicious in-range version.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin to openstacksdk==4.11.0. Add requests as a direct dependency with pinned minimum. Commit uv.lock.

findings.evidence_redacted: if _is_modify_operation_allowed(): return mcp.tool()(func)  # evaluated at import time
findings.impact: Tool registration state is stale if ALLOW_MODIFY_OPERATIONS changes at runtime.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the import-time behavior. Add a startup assertion that the variable is immutable after initialization.

findings.evidence_redacted: "CRITICAL: For create action, both flavor AND image are REQUIRED."  # imperative docstring
findings.impact: Overly prescriptive imperative-tone docstrings can be exploited by prompt injection to embed conflicting instructions.
findings.suggested_fix: Move validation guidance into runtime error messages, not the MCP tool description.

findings.evidence_redacted: # Docstring contains garbled compute-resource code fragment and 'continueate)' token
findings.impact: Indicates file corruption. May mask logic errors and confuse static analysis.
findings.suggested_fix: Clean up the function docstring to remove all embedded code fragments.

findings.evidence_redacted: def get_service_status():  # shadows import at line 17, redefined again at line 951
findings.impact: Security-relevant changes in one implementation may not propagate. Callers may invoke the wrong version silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove duplicate definitions. Use the services.core import exclusively.

findings.evidence_redacted:
return error_msg
logger.error(error_msg)  # unreachable
return error_msg  # unreachable
findings.impact: Unreachable logging means errors are silently dropped in this path, complicating incident debugging.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the two unreachable lines after the first return error_msg.

findings.evidence_redacted: token = conn.identity.get_token()  # token variable never used after this line
findings.impact: Token acquired unnecessarily, increasing its exposure surface in local variable scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the token = ... line entirely.

findings.evidence_redacted: action=trigger_crash_dump  # forces ACPI crash dump (NMI) with no confirm
findings.impact: Triggering a crash dump immediately disrupts the instance and may corrupt in-flight transactions. No confirmation gate exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Add confirm: bool = False gate.

recommendations: Immediate: Remove token fragment from connection.py:118 log statement.
Immediate: Migrate all raw requests.get() calls in services/core.py to OpenStack SDK transport.
Immediate: Add confirm: bool = False gates to all destructive MCP tool actions (delete, force_delete, evacuate, trigger_crash_dump).
Short-term: Default OS_AUTH_PROTOCOL to https; require ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=true as explicit opt-in. Never set verify=False silently.
Short-term: Remove private_key from all tool responses. Implement secure out-of-band delivery.
Short-term: Default REMOTE_AUTH_ENABLE=true for HTTP transport. Require explicit opt-out.
Short-term: Remove email from get_user_list default response; add include_email: bool = False opt-in.
Short-term: Fix validate_resource_ownership to re-raise 401/403 and default to deny on unknown resource state.
Medium-term: Add UUID input validation for all *_id tool parameters before SDK calls.
Medium-term: Add MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 200 constant and paginate all list calls.
Medium-term: Fix duplicate get_service_status definitions, orphaned except block, garbled docstring, dead code in set_keypair.py.
Medium-term: Pin openstacksdk to exact version; add requests as direct dep; commit uv.lock.
Architecture: Separate read-only and write MCP servers with different credentials and auth requirements.
Architecture: Define a data minimization schema enforced at serialization layer (never return private keys, tokens, credential objects, system-scoped role assignments).
Architecture: Adopt HTTPS-first transport policy; require two explicit env-var opt-ins for HTTP deployment.
Architecture: Install gitleaks or detect-secrets as a pre-commit hook to prevent future credential logging.
Architecture: Classify each set_* tool action as read-safe / confirm-required / admin-only and document in tool description.
